These things the Sultan commanded, and he left and went to Egypt;
and he did not wait to meet with the Sheikh.
And when the Sheikh was brought to Damascus,
they brought him into the fortress.
And him, along with the Mongol emir who was with him, they shut up in one chamber,
and the ambassador of the Lord of Mardin in another chamber,
and their servants two by two in a room.
And the youth, the son of the Mongol emir, along with another youth, the son of Majd al-Mulk, they appointed to the service of Malik al-Umara (the Prince of Emirs);
and they rode with him and carried his arms.
And they established a law
that no one should ask his fellow concerning Sheikh Abd al-Rahman,
where he was or how he was.
And news of him was hidden until today,
a space of a full year.
Now after the departure of Sheikh Abd al-Rahman for Syria,
it was reported to Ahmad, the King of Kings, concerning his brother Qunqurtai,
"He has an understanding with Arghun, the son of Abaqa,
and he is preparing to fall upon you one night while you are asleep inside your tent to kill you."
Therefore Ahmad was shaken and terrified,
and in haste he arrested his brother Qunqurtai and killed him.
And Arghun heard of the murder of his uncle,
and he grieved over him greatly,
and his heart was alienated from Ahmad.
And when Ahmad learned
that Arghun's heart was not at peace with him,
he sent against him a certain army commander whose name was Alinak {OCR?} with a large force.
And when Alinak Noyan arrived and reached Khorasan,
Arghun began to flee before him.
And Alinak took the matter lightly {OCR?},
and he neglected the full vigilance of war,
and began to eat and to drink and to get drunk.
And on one of the nights, Arghun attacked the camp of Alinak,
and he made a great slaughter in it;
and with difficulty Alinak was able, along with a few men, to escape from the sword.
Then Ahmad, when he heard of the evil event that had befallen Alinak,
sent to all the countries and gathered forces of Mongols, Kurds, Lors, Persians, and Georgians,
and marched against Arghun into Khorasan.
